note: Rules are written in our own words. Every rule cites at least one U.S. government source. Quotes from CPSC recall notices are checked word for word against data/cpsc/snapshot.json by tests/unit/rules.test.ts; quotes from other government pages record the date they were checked.

home.title: Anchor the {item} to the wall
home.hazard: A child who pulls up on furniture that isn't anchored can tip it over.
home.action: Strap it to a wall stud with an anti-tip kit.

sources.quote: Anchoring all furniture with drawers, doors, and shelves to the wall prevents tip-over injuries and deaths
The recalled dressers are unstable if they are not anchored to the wall, posing tip-over and entrapment hazards that can result in risks of serious injuries or death to children.

home.title: Strap the {item} to the wall
home.hazard: A TV on a stand can come down on a child who pulls on it or the stand.
home.action: Use a TV anti-tip strap on the mounting holes on the back.

sources.quote: If you're anchoring a flat-screen TV, you'll want to use the standard mounting holes on the back of the display.
Anchoring all furniture with drawers, doors, and shelves to the wall prevents tip-over injuries and deaths

home.title: Get the {item} cords out of reach
home.hazard: Long window-covering cords can strangle a young child.
home.action: Wind the cords up high on a cleat now, and plan to switch to cordless.

sources.quote: The recalled blinds have long operating cords that can cause death or serious injury to children, due to strangulation and entanglement hazards.
Consumers should immediately put the window blind's cords up and away from children

home.title: Keep the {item} bare
home.hazard: Pillows, blankets and padding in a sleep space are a suffocation risk.
home.action: Only a fitted sheet in the sleep space, and baby goes down on their back.

sources.quote: Do remember 'Bare is Best' - nothing but a fitted sheet in a crib, bassinet or play yard
Do always place baby on their back

home.title: Take the bumpers out of the {item}
home.hazard: Padded crib bumpers can block a baby's breathing.
home.action: Remove them and don't put them back.

sources.quote: Padded crib bumpers are banned by the federal Safe Sleep for Babies Act.

home.title: Put the {item} out of reach
home.hazard: Swallowed high-powered magnets can pull together inside the gut.
home.action: Store magnet sets up high in a closed container.

sources.quote: When high-powered magnets are swallowed, the ingested magnets can attract each other, or other metal objects, and become lodged in the digestive system.

home.title: Block steps when the {item} is out
home.hazard: Walkers that don't stop at the edge of a step can go down it.
home.action: Only use the walker on one level, away from any step.

sources.quote: fail to stop at the edge of a step, posing a deadly fall hazard

home.title: Buckle the {item} strap every time
home.hazard: Without the crotch strap, a child can slide or climb out of a high chair.
home.action: Use the full restraint every meal, tray or no tray.

sources.quote: sold without the required attached crotch restraint, posing a deadly fall hazard for children

home.title: Use the {item} only while awake and watched
home.hazard: Soft infant cushions can block a baby's breathing.
home.action: Never let the baby sleep on it; move them to the crib.

sources.quote: can obstruct an infant's breathing, posing a serious risk of injury or death from suffocation
Do use products intended for sleep

home.title: Move the baby to the crib if they fall asleep in the {item}
home.hazard: Sleeping at an incline is linked to infant deaths.
home.action: Use it awake only; sleep goes in a flat crib or bassinet.

sources.quote: Infant fatalities have occurred in inclined sleeper products after the infants rolled from their back to their stomach or side while unrestrained

home.title: Keep a hand on the baby in the {item}
home.hazard: Bath seats have tipped over in the water.
home.action: Stay within arm's reach for the whole bath.

sources.quote: they are unstable and can tip over while in use, posing a risk of serious injury or death due to drowning

secondhand.reason: Padded crib bumpers are banned under federal law.

sources.quote: Padded crib bumpers are banned by the federal Safe Sleep for Babies Act.

secondhand.reason: Sleep products with an incline over ten degrees are banned.

sources.quote: The recalled bassinets violate the Safe Sleep for Babies Act because they were marketed for infant sleep and have an incline angle greater than 10 degrees.
